# Midway M90 Chin Turret
The Midway's fixed twin 90mm turret is operated from its dedicated gunnery seat and console. It supports landed physical fire and delayed flare-assisted impacts during transit or CAS flybys. Tactical hover and takeoff do not support M90 gunnery.
## Setup and Controls - While landed, calibrate the hardpoint with a screwdriver, then use a multitool to program your faction IFF. - Buckle into the gunnery seat and take turret control. Mouse movement aims; hold left click to fire. - The turret slews at sixty degrees per second. WASD or the panel arrows pan its camera; the center button recenters. - Landed manual fire has a 225-degree forward arc and a twenty-tile targeting circle. Rounds aimed inside the circle stop at the cursor; outside it they keep traveling until collision. - Normal and Night optics respect opaque walls. Thermal can observe through walls, but physical shells cannot pass through them. - Mark a target or acquire the current priority hostile, then authorize tracked fire for thirty seconds. Marking alone never permits fire. - AR mode shows the turret's targeting boundary in the main view. Return to the gun panel to leave AR.
## Ammunition and Heat - Load crates with a power loader. Feeds one and two accept any M90 crate; feed three is reserved for Squall. - Select a feed or alternate after each shell. Empty feeds automatically fall back to another loaded feed. - Squall contains 2400 kinetic rounds and fires fifteen rounds per second without ejecting casings. It can mark only living targets. - HEAP contains 400 explosive rounds and supports both groundside and airborne fire. - Gale scatter, Ember incendiary, and Tempest devastator are airborne-only explosive feeds. Explosive ammunition fires three shells per second. - Explosive shells heat the barrels faster than Squall. At maximum heat the turret locks until it cools to forty percent. - A feed warns its gunner when it falls below one quarter of its full crate capacity.
## Airborne Flare Fire - Select an active faction signal flare on the right TARGET monitor. Aim within ten tiles of it. - Each shell consumes one round immediately and impacts after a one-to-two-second delay. - Protected overhead cover, incompatible ammunition, and friendly clearance can prevent a shot. - Friendly clearance is checked again at impact. A cancelled delayed impact does not refund its shell. - Clearing or losing the flare stops airborne fire. Nearby players receive a warning when a gunner locks their flare.
## AI Free Fire and IFF - Enable AI free fire explicitly. Groundside AI engages only after landing on the planet, never in a shipside hangar. - Airborne AI scans active flares and compatible feeds, but each new target requires individual gunner approval. - AI cannot acquire or shoot through walls, even with Thermal selected. - Taking manual control pauses AI scanning without disabling it. Disabling AI starts a five-minute reactivation cooldown. - Groundside AI forces IFF on until close self-defense or an overwhelming group returns control to the gunner's toggle. - Disabling IFF removes friendly shot and impact protection.
## Damage and Rebuilding The mount disables at zero integrity. Land before beginning a staged engineer rebuild: - Strip the damaged mechanism with a wrench. - Install one box of 90mm repair parts from the dropship fabricator. - Add ten lengths of cable. - Weld the housing with a lit blowtorch, consuming five fuel. - Calibrate and close it with a screwdriver. Interrupted steps do not advance the repair. A completed rebuild restores full integrity.
